name: Laburito
summary: A geolocated platform that connects people looking for a service with tradespeople: a web app for Seekers, a mobile app for professionals and an admin panel.
description: A geolocated platform that connects Seekers with tradespeople. One Flutter codebase with three surfaces: the Seeker web app, the native app for professionals and a desktop panel to run the platform. Final degree project at USAL (Professional Integration Seminar 2026), planned with IEEE 1058, a risk matrix and burndown.

architecture.presentation: CrearPedidoScreen is a step-by-step form (what, where, photos, validity); CrearPedidoController, generated with riverpod_generator, holds the state.
architecture.domain: freezed models and enums such as PedidoEstado, a Dart mirror of the transitions defined in the database.
architecture.data: PedidosRepository queries Supabase: PostgreSQL with RLS and PostGIS for geolocation.

decisions.title: One codebase, three surfaces
decisions.body: The Seeker web app, the native app for professionals and the admin panel come from the same Flutter project. The panel moderates users, verifies identities, handles reports and reviews, and manages categories, prices and coupons.

decisions.title: The database validates, the app follows
decisions.body: Request states and their transitions live in PostgreSQL. PedidoEstado mirrors them in Dart only to avoid offering buttons the server would reject, and a test checks both tables match.

decisions.title: Keys out of the repository
decisions.body: Supabase and Google Maps keys come in through --dart-define from an uncommitted .env. If they are missing, the app still starts and shows what to fill in instead of crashing.

decisions.title: Places API over HTTP
decisions.body: Autocomplete and geocoding are called from Dart, so the key is restricted by API rather than by app. In production there would be two keys, one per kind of use.

mediaCaptions.burndown-sprint-03: Project burndown at the end of Sprint 3: ideal, planned and actual.
